title: Tier 1 plugin wiring — survival reflexes below deliberation
recordedAt: 2026-07-28T13:44:00Z (take 2 — correct monitor MSI MAG323UPF + audio, owner-fixed OBS scene)
scenario: Standalone drill bot (skill_drill) with the U13 plugin set (mineflayer-auto-eat 3.3.6, mineflayer-armor-manager 2.0.1, pathfinder) joined the LIVE world alongside the 6-villager fleet. RCON gave 8 bread and applied minecraft:hunger 15s/amp200; iron helmet+chestplate given mid-run.

evidence.autoEat: PROVEN on camera (take 2): REFLEX_autoeat_started fired at food=16 — the exact configured startAt threshold — then ~8 eat cycles against the active hunger effect; ended food 19/20. Zero LLM/deliberation involvement (fleet untouched, zero tokens).
evidence.armorManager: NEGATIVE FINDING (take 2, direct armor-slot poll): iron helmet+chestplate given via /give were picked up but armor-manager's auto-equip never moved them to armor slots during the run. This validates the repo's original design choice — the hand-rolled ArmorWatcher POLLS instead of trusting the plugin's playerCollect trigger. U13's wiring keeps equipAll() at connect only; recommendation for assembly: keep PLUGIN_ARMOR_MANAGER=0 (hand-rolled fallback) until the plugin's trigger is characterized, or add a periodic equipAll nudge.

caveats: Drill bot replicates the U13 wiring path standalone; the deployed minecraft-service container still runs pre-merge code. Service-level proof lands when the container is rebuilt (up -d --build --no-deps minecraft-service), which drops and respawns the fleet — deferred to avoid disturbing the live run.
One real interop bug found and fixed during filming: auto-eat 3.3.6 CJS default import is {plugin}, not a callable — exactly the drift class the demo gate exists to catch.
